title: Luke 10: The Seventy Sent and the Good Samaritan
body:
Read the chapter → [Luke 10](/bible/luke/10)

## Introduction

This session covers Luke 10 through 13. The video it comes from is titled for John 6 through 9, but the reading given is Luke, and it is Luke that these notes follow. The seventy are sent out two and two, a lawyer is answered with the parable of the good Samaritan, the disciples are taught how to pray, the woes are pronounced upon the Pharisees and the lawyers, and the last chapter closes over Jerusalem. The thread is repentance and the discerning of the time.

**[Luke 10:1-2](/bible/luke/10#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/luke/10#v1)</sup> After these things the Lord appointed other seventy also, and sent them two and two before his face into every city and place, whither he himself would come.
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/luke/10#v2)</sup> Therefore said he unto them, The harvest truly is great, but the labourers are few: pray ye therefore the Lord of the harvest, that he would send forth labourers into his harvest.

- The Lord appointed other seventy also, and sent them two and two before his face into every city and place whither he himself would come.
- The harvest truly is great, but the labourers are few: pray ye therefore the Lord of the harvest, that he would send forth labourers into his harvest.

**[Luke 10:3-4](/bible/luke/10#v3)**

> <sup>[3](/bible/luke/10#v3)</sup> Go your ways: behold, I send you forth as lambs among wolves.
>
> <sup>[4](/bible/luke/10#v4)</sup> Carry neither purse, nor scrip, nor shoes: and salute no man by the way.

- Behold, I send you forth as lambs among wolves. Carry neither purse, nor scrip, nor shoes: and salute no man by the way.

**[Luke 10:5-7](/bible/luke/10#v5)**

> <sup>[5](/bible/luke/10#v5)</sup> And into whatsoever house ye enter, first say, Peace be to this house.
>
> <sup>[6](/bible/luke/10#v6)</sup> And if the son of peace be there, your peace shall rest upon it: if not, it shall turn to you again.
>
> <sup>[7](/bible/luke/10#v7)</sup> And in the same house remain, eating and drinking such things as they give: for the labourer is worthy of his hire. Go not from house to house.

- Into whatsoever house ye enter, first say, Peace be to this house, and if the son of peace be there, your peace shall rest upon it.
- In the same house remain, eating and drinking such things as they give: for the labourer is worthy of his hire. Go not from house to house.

**[Luke 10:8-9](/bible/luke/10#v8)**

> <sup>[8](/bible/luke/10#v8)</sup> And into whatsoever city ye enter, and they receive you, eat such things as are set before you:
>
> <sup>[9](/bible/luke/10#v9)</sup> And heal the sick that are therein, and say unto them, The kingdom of God is come nigh unto you.

- Heal the sick that are therein, and say unto them, The kingdom of God is come nigh unto you.
- That word is said to a house that received them. Where there is charity and brotherhood enough to take a labourer in, the kingdom is near to that house.

**[Luke 10:10-12](/bible/luke/10#v10)**

> <sup>[10](/bible/luke/10#v10)</sup> But into whatsoever city ye enter, and they receive you not, go your ways out into the streets of the same, and say,
>
> <sup>[11](/bible/luke/10#v11)</sup> Even the very dust of your city, which cleaveth on us, we do wipe off against you: notwithstanding be ye sure of this, that the kingdom of God is come nigh unto you.
>
> <sup>[12](/bible/luke/10#v12)</sup> But I say unto you, that it shall be more tolerable in that day for Sodom, than for that city.

- Where they are not received, they wipe off the very dust of the city, and it shall be more tolerable in that day for Sodom than for that city.

**[Luke 10:13-16](/bible/luke/10#v13)**

> <sup>[13](/bible/luke/10#v13)</sup> Woe unto thee, Chorazin! woe unto thee, Bethsaida! for if the mighty works had been done in Tyre and Sidon, which have been done in you, they had a great while ago repented, sitting in sackcloth and ashes.
>
> <sup>[14](/bible/luke/10#v14)</sup> But it shall be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon at the judgment, than for you.
>
> <sup>[15](/bible/luke/10#v15)</sup> And thou, Capernaum, which art exalted to heaven, shalt be thrust down to hell.
>
> <sup>[16](/bible/luke/10#v16)</sup> He that heareth you heareth me; and he that despiseth you despiseth me; and he that despiseth me despiseth him that sent me.

- Woe unto thee, Chorazin! woe unto thee, Bethsaida! If the mighty works had been done in Tyre and Sidon which have been done in you, they had a great while ago repented, sitting in sackcloth and ashes.
- Other nations would have turned at what Israel watched and did not turn at. That is what a stiffnecked people looks like.
- He that heareth you heareth me; and he that despiseth you despiseth me; and he that despiseth me despiseth him that sent me.

**[Luke 10:17-20](/bible/luke/10#v17)**

> <sup>[17](/bible/luke/10#v17)</sup> And the seventy returned again with joy, saying, Lord, even the devils are subject unto us through thy name.
>
> <sup>[18](/bible/luke/10#v18)</sup> And he said unto them, I beheld Satan as lightning fall from heaven.
>
> <sup>[19](/bible/luke/10#v19)</sup> Behold, I give unto you power to tread on serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy: and nothing shall by any means hurt you.
>
> <sup>[20](/bible/luke/10#v20)</sup> Notwithstanding in this rejoice not, that the spirits are subject unto you; but rather rejoice, because your names are written in heaven.

- The seventy return with joy that even the devils are subject unto them, and he answers, I beheld Satan as lightning fall from heaven.
- Behold, I give unto you power to tread on serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy: and nothing shall by any means hurt you.
- Notwithstanding in this rejoice not, that the spirits are subject unto you; but rather rejoice, because your names are written in heaven.

**[Luke 10:21-22](/bible/luke/10#v21)**

> <sup>[21](/bible/luke/10#v21)</sup> In that hour Jesus rejoiced in spirit, and said, I thank thee, O Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent, and hast revealed them unto babes: even so, Father; for so it seemed good in thy sight.
>
> <sup>[22](/bible/luke/10#v22)</sup> All things are delivered to me of my Father: and no man knoweth who the Son is, but the Father; and who the Father is, but the Son, and he to whom the Son will reveal him.

- I thank thee, O Father, that thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent, and hast revealed them unto babes.
- No man knoweth who the Son is, but the Father; and who the Father is, but the Son, and he to whom the Son will reveal him. A man does not know the Father apart from the son.

**[Luke 10:23-24](/bible/luke/10#v23)**

> <sup>[23](/bible/luke/10#v23)</sup> And he turned him unto his disciples, and said privately, Blessed are the eyes which see the things that ye see:
>
> <sup>[24](/bible/luke/10#v24)</sup> For I tell you, that many prophets and kings have desired to see those things which ye see, and have not seen them; and to hear those things which ye hear, and have not heard them.

- Blessed are the eyes which see the things that ye see. Many prophets and kings have desired to see those things which ye see, and have not seen them.
- The prophets wrote of these things and did not see the time of them.

  Precepts:
  - **[1 Peter 1:10-11](/bible/1-peter/1#v10)**
    > <sup>[10](/bible/1-peter/1#v10)</sup> Of which salvation the prophets have enquired and searched diligently, who prophesied of the grace that should come unto you:
    >
    > <sup>[11](/bible/1-peter/1#v11)</sup> Searching what, or what manner of time the Spirit of Christ which was in them did signify, when it testified beforehand the sufferings of Christ, and the glory that should follow.

    The prophets have enquired and searched diligently, searching what manner of time the Spirit of Christ which was in them did signify.

**[Luke 10:25-28](/bible/luke/10#v25)**

> <sup>[25](/bible/luke/10#v25)</sup> And, behold, a certain lawyer stood up, and tempted him, saying, Master, what shall I do to inherit eternal life?
>
> <sup>[26](/bible/luke/10#v26)</sup> He said unto him, What is written in the law? how readest thou?
>
> <sup>[27](/bible/luke/10#v27)</sup> And he answering said, Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy strength, and with all thy mind; and thy neighbour as thyself.
>
> <sup>[28](/bible/luke/10#v28)</sup> And he said unto him, Thou hast answered right: this do, and thou shalt live.

- A lawyer stands up and asks what he shall do to inherit eternal life, and is sent to the law: What is written in the law? how readest thou?
- Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and thy neighbour as thyself. Thou hast answered right: this do, and thou shalt live.

**[Luke 10:29-37](/bible/luke/10#v29)**

> <sup>[29](/bible/luke/10#v29)</sup> But he, willing to justify himself, said unto Jesus, And who is my neighbour?
>
> <sup>[30](/bible/luke/10#v30)</sup> And Jesus answering said, A certain man went down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and fell among thieves, which stripped him of his raiment, and wounded him, and departed, leaving him half dead.
>
> <sup>[31](/bible/luke/10#v31)</sup> And by chance there came down a certain priest that way: and when he saw him, he passed by on the other side.
>
> <sup>[32](/bible/luke/10#v32)</sup> And likewise a Levite, when he was at the place, came and looked on him, and passed by on the other side.
>
> <sup>[33](/bible/luke/10#v33)</sup> But a certain Samaritan, as he journeyed, came where he was: and when he saw him, he had compassion on him,
>
> <sup>[34](/bible/luke/10#v34)</sup> And went to him, and bound up his wounds, pouring in oil and wine, and set him on his own beast, and brought him to an inn, and took care of him.
>
> <sup>[35](/bible/luke/10#v35)</sup> And on the morrow when he departed, he took out two pence, and gave them to the host, and said unto him, Take care of him; and whatsoever thou spendest more, when I come again, I will repay thee.
>
> <sup>[36](/bible/luke/10#v36)</sup> Which now of these three, thinkest thou, was neighbour unto him that fell among the thieves?
>
> <sup>[37](/bible/luke/10#v37)</sup> And he said, He that shewed mercy on him. Then said Jesus unto him, Go, and do thou likewise.

- Willing to justify himself, he asks, And who is my neighbour?
- A priest and a Levite pass by on the other side. Both were of the southern kingdom, and neither had mercy on their own.
- A Samaritan had compassion, bound up his wounds, and paid for his keeping. Samaria was the head of Ephraim, so the man who showed mercy was of the northern kingdom.
- Go, and do thou likewise. The mercy that was withheld between the two houses is the very thing commanded here.

  Precepts:
  - **[Isaiah 7:9](/bible/isaiah/7#v9)**
    > <sup>[9](/bible/isaiah/7#v9)</sup> And the head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is Remaliah’s son. If ye will not believe, surely ye shall not be established.

    The head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is Remaliah's son.

**[Luke 10:38-42](/bible/luke/10#v38)**

> <sup>[38](/bible/luke/10#v38)</sup> Now it came to pass, as they went, that he entered into a certain village: and a certain woman named Martha received him into her house.
>
> <sup>[39](/bible/luke/10#v39)</sup> And she had a sister called Mary, which also sat at Jesus’ feet, and heard his word.
>
> <sup>[40](/bible/luke/10#v40)</sup> But Martha was cumbered about much serving, and came to him, and said, Lord, dost thou not care that my sister hath left me to serve alone? bid her therefore that she help me.
>
> <sup>[41](/bible/luke/10#v41)</sup> And Jesus answered and said unto her, Martha, Martha, thou art careful and troubled about many things:
>
> <sup>[42](/bible/luke/10#v42)</sup> But one thing is needful: and Mary hath chosen that good part, which shall not be taken away from her.

- Martha was cumbered about much serving and asked that Mary be told to help her; Mary sat at his feet and heard his word.
- Mary hath chosen that good part, which shall not be taken away from her. A man can be so taken up with the business of the day that the word never gets in him.
